subject: HarborHealth: temporary ephemera retention carve-out and evidence matrix
messages:
From: Samantha Li <samantha.li@harborhealth.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: security@harborhealth.com
Date: 2026-08-24T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: temporary exemption for ephemeral debug logs (HarborHealth)

Hi Logan,

Quick introduction — I'm Samantha on HarborHealth's security team. We're running a pilot of conversational assistants for a subset of patients and have a narrow requirement: debug session traces (ephemeral, per-tenant) need to be retained for 90 days for a short investigative period, whereas Redwood's default is 30 days.

Before we start the pilot we'd like to request a temporary, tenant-scoped retention carve-out for these traces for 90 days (30 -> 90) and need evidence to satisfy our auditors:
- CAIQ / SIG mapping showing where tenant-scoped session logs are controlled and deleted
- SOC 2 attestable evidence of deletion workflows (sample deletion logs or proof-of-delete artifacts)
- Retention-playbook excerpt describing deletion process and escalation path
- Any compensating controls (access gating, masked storage, time-bound access tokens) that reduce risk during extended retention

Can you confirm:
1) Whether Redwood can make a tenant-specific retention exception for HarborHealth for the pilot window (90 days)
2) What evidence you can provide and an estimated delivery timeline (we'd like this by 2026-08-28ET if possible)

We may need a short exceptions addendum to our contract if this proceeds — happy to loop procurement.

Thanks,
Samantha Li
Senior Security Analyst
HarborHealth

Hi Samantha — thanks for the clear ask and timeline. Looping in Priya from Security and Karthik from Platform so we can put together a focused evidence pack. Quick summary of how we intend to approach this: 

- Confirm feasibility: Karthik to confirm the tenant-scoped retention configuration and whether we can apply a 90-day TTL to the specified tenant IDs for the pilot window.
- Evidence pack: Priya to prepare CAIQ excerpts, a short deletion proof template (proof-of-delete artifacts), and the retention playbook excerpt.
- Compensating controls: we'll provide the access gating controls in place (RBAC, time-limited SAS tokens for debug exports, and masking practices).

Proposed timeline: we can aim to deliver an initial evidence matrix and playbook excerpt by 2026-08-27 (US-PST). If HarborHealth needs it sooner for an auditor call on 2026-08-28, we'll prioritize.

Next steps for you: can you confirm the tenant identifiers (or a sample tenant id) and whether PII will be included in the debug traces? That will affect the evidence detail we include.

I'll treat this as a scoped, time-bound exception (pilot only) and we'll draft a short addendum if approved.

Best,
Logan Wright
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Request: temporary exemption for ephemeral debug logs (HarborHealth)

Hi Samantha — thanks for the details. I pulled together an evidence-first response below and attached the initial artifacts. See the attached spreadsheet for a compact CAIQ->artifact mapping. High level: 

1) Tenant-specific retention: feasible. We support tenant-scoped TTL overrides at the routing layer; Karthik has validated we can schedule a 60/90-day TTL for a small set of tenant IDs for a defined window. We'll implement as a targeted config flag and schedule automatic rollback to 30 days after the pilot end date.

2) Evidence deliverables (attached):
- harbor_evidence_matrix_v1.xlsx: maps CAIQ/SIG questions -> Redwood artifacts (policy excerpts, playbook anchors, log sample IDs)
- retention-playbook-excerpt.pdf: excerpt showing the deletion runbook and verification steps (proof-of-delete generation is part of the runbook)
- sample-ephemeral-logs.txt: redacted sample of a session trace with PII tokenization applied

3) Proof-of-delete model: our deletion job writes a signed proof file (hashed manifest + timestamp) into an internal evidence store and emits an audit event (audit-id). We can provide a redacted example proof-of-delete artifact and the SHA256 manifest on request.

4) Compensating controls and mitigations while TTL extended:
- Tenant-limited access only (RBAC + least privilege)
- Encrypted-at-rest with tenant-scoped KMS key access control
- Short-lived console and API tokens for debug exports; activity logged to audit trail
- Rolling sampling of retained traces for manual review to detect PII leakage

Implementation and timing: Karthik, can you confirm scheduling the TTL change to 90 days for HarborHealth tenant IDs and the rollback automation? If yes, we can provision the evidence pack by EOD 2026-08-27.

Regards,
Priya Natarajan
Principal Security Engineer, Redwood Inference

- We will send the sample tenant IDs in a separate, encrypted message by EOD today.
- Can Redwood also provide the proof-of-delete artifact template (hashed manifest example) so our auditors can validate the format?
- Procurement: we do need a short exceptions addendum outlining scope (tenant IDs, dates, rollback), responsible owners, and acceptance criteria. Can your team draft a one-page addendum (PDF) for signature? We can route through DocuSign.

If you can provide the proof-of-delete example and a draft addendum by tomorrow (2026-08-27), we can proceed to approval and sign the addendum via DocuSign. Thanks again for the fast turnaround.
